statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. NQ extended its European drift to a fresh 31,217.25 session low and has since recovered about 52 points off it, so the directional read persists while a genuine retracement keeps Tail at 21 in the watch band. A 0.96% range, VIX at 15.78 and broad weakness across gold and bitcoin leave the amplifier stack incomplete ahead of the 18:00Z FOMC minutes.
recommendation: Tail remains in the watch band and well below the block threshold. The narrow evidence-based danger window spans the 17:00Z 10-year note auction, the 18:00Z September FOMC minutes and the hours of possible delayed yield-led repricing into the 20:00Z cash close, where the published forecast reaches the elevated band.
headline: NQ extends to a fresh 31,217.25 session low but retraces about 52 points off it, holding Tail at 21 while a 5.70% 30-year yield and firm oil keep Stress elevated into the FOMC minutes
body:
NQ December futures trade near 31,269.50, down 213.75 points or 0.68%, against a 31,483.25 previous close and an open around 31,473.50 to 31,510.00. The session range is 31,217.25 to 31,521.00, roughly 304 points or 0.96%. The material change from the previous hour is two-sided. The 31,251.00 low published then has been taken out, so the European lower-low sequence has extended again, but price now sits about 52 points above the new 31,217.25 extreme rather than pinned to it. A genuine retracement off the session low is exactly the evidence that distinguishes a shallow drift from a pathological no-retracement path, so Tail holds at 21 in the watch band instead of building toward the block threshold.

The amplifier stack remains incomplete. Magnitude is ordinary for a full European session at a 0.96% range and a 0.68% decline. VIX at 15.78 is up 5.13% and has traded a 15.21 to 16.01 range, but 15.78 is low in absolute terms and shows no volatility expansion. The decline is also broad rather than a tech-specific squeeze: Dow futures are down 0.77%, Russell 2000 futures 0.82% and S&P 500 futures 0.41%, with gold down 1.05% and bitcoin down 3.20%. Simultaneous weakness in equities, gold and crypto is consistent with a real-yield and liquidity repricing rather than a directional index squeeze, and softer small-cap breadth raises Stress more than Tail under the risk contract.

The cross-asset backdrop is the main Stress input. The 30-year Treasury yield has reached 5.70%, the highest since 2002, and the 10-year sits near 5.27% after printing 5.31% on 5 October per the Federal Reserve H.15 release. WTI is near 90.02, up 0.65%, and Brent near 101.99, up 1.4%, recovering from five-week lows on Middle East energy-flow risk. High long-end yields together with firm energy are a recognised drag on long-duration growth and AI-related index weight, which is why Stress rises a point to 52 while Tail is unchanged.

The scheduled catalyst stack is concentrated in the U.S. afternoon. The 15:00Z consumer inflation-expectations print, the 17:00Z 10-year note auction and the 18:00Z minutes of the September 15-16 FOMC meeting fall inside the session, with consumer credit at 19:00Z. September delivered the first Federal Reserve rate increase since 2023, so the minutes are a structurally multi-stage interpretation risk in which the bond market can reprice first and equities follow with a delayed second leg. Reporting places roughly 20% odds on a further increase at the October meeting. None of that is observed yet, so under the risk contract event importance raises conditional Tail inside the narrow danger window and Stress across it, without lifting the current reading.

Evidence quality is good but not complete. Live NQ price and range are confirmed from two independent quote sources, VIX, gold, oil and cross-asset futures are current, the long-end yield level is corroborated by current reporting, and the seven-day U.S. calendar is verified. The H.15 release only extends through 5 October, and the shared Finviz context file in this repository carries a 29 September collection timestamp with partial collection status, so it is stale under the 90-minute freshness rule and was not used as evidence. Confidence therefore holds at 87.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours of published Claude assessments stayed in the mapped EA_ON state apart from two WATCH hours at 15:00Z and 16:00Z on 6 October, when Tail reached 22 and 20 during the U.S. cash session, and the 11:00Z hour today, when Tail stepped to 21. Tail decayed from the high teens to a flat 10 through the 6 October evening and the Asian hours, then built through 12, 14 and 21 as the European morning drift developed. Stress held in a 45 to 51 elevated band throughout and Confidence stayed between 86 and 88, so the published record describes a stable regime that has only just begun to deteriorate. Dominant mode was recorded as trend-up through the 6 October cash session, mixed from 20:00Z onward, and trend-down in the most recent hour.
outlookSummary: Tail is expected to hold at 21 while the observed retracement off the session low keeps the drift shallow, then build to 22 into the 13:30Z cash open and 23 in the first full cash hour, where opening-auction continuation with failed pullbacks is the primary conditional path. The 15:00Z inflation-expectations print and the pre-auction lull ease it back through 22 to 21, the 17:00Z 10-year note auction lifts it to 23, and the 18:00Z FOMC minutes and the 19:00Z delayed second leg carry the highest conditional Tail at 26 and 27, crossing into the elevated band and the orange mapped state for those two slots only. The window returns to 23 into the 20:00Z cash close, then decays to 18 post-close and to a 12 to 16 overnight baseline across the Asian and European hours of 8 October, ending ahead of the 12:30Z jobless claims. Stress tracks the same shape between 46 and 58 without leaving the elevated band, and Confidence steps down from 87 to 80 as this assessment's live price-path evidence ages.
